page.title: Writing charts
page.description: Write an actor's behaviour as an SCXML chart in JavaScript, and compile your charts into one image a host runs.

hero.headline: Write chart logic in JavaScript.
hero.lede: A chart's conditions, data and scripts are plain JavaScript that reads the actor's variables by name. Your charts compile into one image: bytes a host runs, in this process or another.

section.heading: Declare variables and read the event.
section.p: Declare an actor's variables with <data>. Each expr is evaluated once, when the actor starts, unless spawn's params give another value.
Every cond, expr, <log expr> and <script> reads the variables by name, beside the names the host sets:

row.cell: the event being handled: name, data, type ('external', 'internal' or 'platform'), sendid, origin, origintype, invokeid, and raw when an I/O processor's answer gave one
the actor's session, as a string
the actor's name, or its chart's name when it has none
the I/O processors, by type; _ioprocessors.scxml.location is the actor's address

section.p: An expression is ordinary JavaScript, such as the spread and slice that keep the thermostat's last three readings below.
An assignment to an undeclared name, to _event or to a system variable raises error.execution, as a throwing expression does.
One region of this thermostat switches the heater while the other logs readings. Its typo event assigns to a name it never declared:

example.code: heater off 18°C, last 18, heating: false heater on 19°C, last 18 19, heating: true 21°C, last 18 19 21, heating: false heater off that was an error.execution

section.p: Inside an attribute, XML needs < for < and & for &.
Both regions of the <parallel> handle a reading in one step. The states it leaves are exited first, then every transition's actions run, then the new states are entered.
So In('on') in the recorder is true only when the heater stays on. At 18°C the recorder logs heating: false before the heater logs heater on.

section.heading: Define helper functions once per chart.
section.p: A function in a chart-level <script> is a helper, made once for the chart and callable from its actors' expressions. This basket prices its items with one:
A helper sees no actor's variables by name, so pass it what it reads, as the basket passes each sku. Another chart cannot call it.
A hibernated, migrated or snapshotted actor gets its helpers back from its chart, not from its blob.
A function held in a variable is not a value, so it keeps its actor in memory. Declare it with function in a chart-level script instead.
<script> also runs statements in a transition, in <onentry> or <onexit>. A chart-level script's other statements run once, when an actor starts.
A host runs chart code in one engine, its datamodel: native by default, or quickjs. On native, a host's actors share one context, and a script's top-level declarations mean this:

item.text: a helper of the chart, as above.
that run's own, gone when the script ends.
a variable of the actor, as a <data> is. It is read before the script runs and written back after, so it keeps its value between runs and is hibernated with the actor.
refused: the script is error.execution each time it runs. Inside a block or a function they are fine.

section.p: compileCharts warns of every top-level var, let, const and class at the script's line, an error with {warningsAsErrors: true}.
The warning names the <data id> to declare instead, which other SCXML tools read. It is the same whichever datamodel a host runs the chart on.
On quickjs a chart-level script runs as global code in the actor's own context, which costs memory. All its declarations are the actor's, and its functions see its variables.

section.heading: Send an event to any actor.
section.p: <send> sends an event to the actor itself, to another actor, or out of the host to your program. Each attribute has an ...expr form that computes it:

row.cell: the actor itself, at the back of its queue
the send's id, for <cancel> and the answer's _event.sendid; idlocation names a declared <data> that gets a generated id, unique in the actor's session only (every session's first is send.1)
variables whose names and values become the data

section.p: The data is <param name expr>s and namelist, as an object, or one <content expr>, any value.
#_internal puts the event in the actor's internal queue, which runs before anything waiting outside, as <raise> does.
This sender sends an order to itself, a note to its internal queue, and a greeting to a target it computes. The note runs before the order sent ahead of it:

example.code: the order went out as send.1 receiver got hello.tea self.note (internal) undefined self.order (external) {"qty":2,"sku":"tea"}

section.p: idlocation must name a declared <data>, as every assignment must. Otherwise the <send> fails with error.execution and nothing is sent.

section.heading: Keep XML data in a variable.
section.p: A <data> whose content is XML holds a document. Node.js and Bun have no DOMParser, so the package builds a small DOM of its own:

item.text: has nodeType, nodeName, nodeValue, attributes, childNodes, firstChild, lastChild, parentNode and textContent, and the methods getElementsByTagName(name) (an array, '*' for every element), getAttribute(name) and hasAttribute(name).

section.p: This menu walks its catalog's price elements with <foreach> and logs each one's sku and text:
An actor whose variable holds a DOM stays in memory: hibernation and snapshots refuse it.
A DOM reaches your program as XML text, in a send's <content> or from actorContext, on both datamodels. A document arrives as the text it was read from, a node written out.

section.heading: Start a child actor from a state.
section.p: <invoke src> starts a child, an actor of another chart, when its state is entered. Leaving the state stops it.
The <param>s set the child's variables, as spawn's params do. The child sends to its parent with target="#_parent".
A child's events carry the invoke's id as _event.invokeid. When the child reaches a final state, the parent gets done.invoke.<id> with its <donedata>.
This parent passes its worker 21; the worker reports progress, then finishes with twice that:

example.code: progress from worker: halfway the worker answered 42

section.p: A parent sends to its child with target="#_worker": #_ and the invoke's id. An <invoke> of a type other than SCXML is a service your program runs ().

section.heading: Wait for the child before sending to it.
section.p: A child starts at the end of the macrostep that entered its state, once the actor settles, as SCXML starts invocations.
Until then a send to the child gets error.communication. That covers the state's own <onentry>, and anything else in the same macrostep:

item.text: a history state that re-enters several states at once.

section.p: Send once the child's first message arrives, such as ready below. Pass what the child needs at its start as a <param>, evaluated when it starts.
This parent sends hello from its <onentry>, from a raised event and after ready. Only the last arrives:

example.code: no child yet: error.communication no child yet: error.communication the child got hello

section.heading: Put several charts in one image.
section.p: compileCharts takes a list of documents, each { name, text }, and compiles them into one image.
Each chart is known by its <scxml name>: host.spawn(name) starts one, and host.chart(name) finds its current version. A document's name is what error messages and src attributes name.
A chart may read another document through src: <invoke src>, <script src> or <data src>. A document in the list answers a src with its name.
For any other src, give compileCharts a resolver, a function (base, source) => text the compile calls. base is the document that names the src.
A resolver may read a file or a database; this one reads a map. Its ResolveError becomes a compile error at the line and column it gives:

example.code: compiled true missing.scxml:1:1: error: parent.scxml asks for missing.scxml, which is not in the store

section.p: Any other error a resolver throws, such as a file it cannot read, is thrown from compileCharts as it is.

section.heading: Compile a whole directory of charts.
section.p: compileDir(dir) compiles every *.scxml file under dir into one image. dir is a path, or a file: URL such as new URL('./charts/', import.meta.url).
Each chart is named by its path under dir, /-separated, and the list is sorted by name. So the first is the image's default boot chart.
A src that names no file of the list is read relative to the directory of the document that names it. orders/order.scxml asking for payment.scxml reads <dir>/orders/payment.scxml.
compileDir reads each such src with a resolver confined to dir, which reports these as compile errors:

item.text: a path that leaves dir: .. past it, an absolute path, or a symbolic link that points outside;
a file that does not exist;
a file that is not UTF-8.

section.p: Another error of the file system, such as no permission, is thrown as it is. A directory with no chart is refused with InvalidError.
compileDir(dir, { resolver }) reads each src with your resolver instead.
An order here invokes the payment chart beside it. Rewritten to reach outside the directory, it no longer compiles:

example.code: paying ../../etc/passwd (from orders/order.scxml) leaves the charts' directory

section.p: A document the resolver read is named by its src as written. A src inside it is read relative to that name's directory.

section.heading: Save an image to run it elsewhere.
section.p: compileCharts returns an object whose image is a Buffer, copied out at its first read and then yours. Its diagnostics lists the compiler's warnings.
Write the image to a file and give it to a host in another process: new Host(readFileSync(path), options).
new Host(compiled, options) copies the image, so close() may free the compiler's memory at once. The garbage collector frees it otherwise.
new Host takes one image or a list, compile results and bytes alike. Each becomes a segment, the number the host knows it by, in order.
host.addImage(bytes) adds an image to a running host. It copies the bytes and returns the image's segment.

section.heading: Boot named actors from a manifest.
section.p: When a system starts the same actors every time, list them in a manifest, so your program need not know which.
A manifest is a <system> document. Its charts are <chart name src>, read through the resolver, and its actors <actor name chart>.
compileSystem compiles it, and host.boot(segment) spawns its actors, each with its name. The image new Host was given first is segment 0.
A program that spawns its own actors can skip boot. An image from compileCharts has one boot actor too, of its first chart, named after its <scxml name>.
